name: Ivan Ibrahim

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What is an ordinary working day like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am Ivan, 43. A shop owner often sends the till report before the invoices, so I line them up, run an AI check, and show Mara where a number does not match. I have a bachelor’s degree in accounting and am still a junior here, learning the tax rules I missed after years in my family’s shop; I like finding a pattern, but a late correction keeps me at my desk.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What are your home finances and technology habits?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Leila works part time at a clinic, and our children Sami and Lina are both in school. We have a mortgage, but this firm pays my junior work well, and we have around ten months of expenses saved with plenty of other accounting firms nearby. I use AI every day for first checks, then compare each flag with a receipt before Mara signs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could picture the same pile of late receipts with a quicker search button. The tax deadline would still be Friday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team that a small tool can catch repeated invoices but a person still checks the source. I use AI every day already, and I make the corrections before my supervisor signs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I feel secure here because my junior post pays unusually well, we have roughly ten months of expenses saved, and many firms are nearby. I am still learning tax rules, but the work and mortgage look steady in this picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the shop accounts under my supervisor Mara and use my daily AI check against the scanned invoices. Each monthly payday I would move fifty into the household reserve until it reaches a full year of expenses, rather than spend it on a bigger car.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about income and the house. I would still worry about an uncorrected tax error more than the software itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the checker catch this week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A client sent the same till receipt twice, and the tool marked both. I checked the original scan and removed one before the tax return went to Mara.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a full year of savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Leila and I have two children and a mortgage, so I like a long runway. Fifty a month is new money from pay, not a claim that our present reserve is growing by itself.

say: I would say **duplicate detection** helps if someone checks the original receipt.
I would tell colleagues my **daily AI check** still ends with Mara’s human sign-off.
think: My **high junior pay** and ten-month reserve make the mortgage feel secure.
I am still learning **tax rules**, so I keep the source beside every flag.
do: Keep checking **shop invoices** against daily AI flags under Mara’s review.
Transfer **fifty monthly** from pay until the reserve covers a year.
feel: I feel **calm** about income and the house.

fieldNote: He uses AI **daily** but personally verifies duplicates before a supervisor signs.
A new **fifty-monthly deposit** aims to lift an already strong reserve to one full year.

steps.text: Keep verifying AI flags against shop invoices under Mara’s review
Transfer fifty monthly from pay until reserve covers one year

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The first draft and check could be done in minutes instead of hours. That would test whether the firm still wants a junior on each file.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say we should measure errors as well as speed before cutting the review rota. I would ask Mara to let juniors see the mistakes the tool makes, because learning only from clean output is a poor apprenticeship.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own paid hours could shrink as routine tax returns get cheaper, even though I am quick with AI. Ten months of savings and plenty of local firms give me room to search, but high current pay may be hard to match.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I would join the firm’s paid AI quality course if a place is confirmed, then test its approved checker on old returns without client details. If my paid hours fall in the first year, I would apply for advertised quality-review posts only when the written salary and start date keep our mortgage covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, though I can act before the cash runs out. A tool can make my desk efficient and still make the desk smaller.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no course place?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my present accounts and use the firm’s free training examples after work. I would not assume a course request is the same as learning the new system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a large pay cut elsewhere?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on a guess about a safer title. I would compare the written offer with our fixed bills and make a move only after the start date is agreed.

I would say juniors need to inspect **tool mistakes** to learn their trade.
think: My **paid hours** could fall despite daily AI use.
A ten-month reserve helps, but another firm may not match my **high pay**.
do: Take the **paid quality course** if seated; use free examples while keeping current accounts otherwise.
Test the approved checker on **anonymised old returns**.
Apply for **written-pay quality posts** if hours fall and a start date covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a smaller paid desk.
S1.quote: A tool can make my desk efficient and still make the desk smaller.
fieldNote: He embraces a **quality test** but recognises AI fluency does not guarantee junior hours.
His external move needs a **written offer** and agreed start date because current pay is high.

steps.text: Take paid course if seated; use free examples while employed; test approved checker on anonymised returns

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years would come before I finish learning the harder tax cases. Robots around 2031 would not protect my screen job in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients that a named accountant must still answer for a return when AGI prepares it in 2028. I would not tell coworkers that being fast with AI guarantees a paid seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior tax post to disappear or lose most of its pay when cheap thinking work arrives. Our ten-month reserve is strong, but Leila’s part-time clinic wage and the mortgage would make a long search painful.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would redirect the monthly car-upgrade saving into a new cash job-loss account and ask Mara about paid on-site stock-count work for clients. If I lose the accounting post in the first year after 2028, I would take a posted paid stock-count contract only if its hours and start date cover childcare, while applying to advertised accountant vacancies only with written pay that covers our fixed bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect the work I am paid well to do to go. I can search and pay the mortgage for months, but I cannot make a good offer appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is stock counting a permanent route?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, capable robots around 2031 could reach the physical stock checks too. I would treat a contract as a bridge and keep looking for paid work rather than call it safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Leila about the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner Leila that the bigger car can wait and the monthly transfer now protects our mortgage. We would keep the car that gets the children to school.

say: I would ask for a **named return signer** when AGI reaches accounts in 2028.
I would say robots around **2031** do not keep tax desks open.
think: I expect my **junior tax pay** to vanish or shrink sharply.
Ten months saved helps, but Leila’s wage cannot carry a long **mortgage gap**.
do: Redirect monthly **car-upgrade deposits** into new job-loss cash.
Take a **posted paid stock-count contract** after job loss only with workable childcare and start date.
Apply for **advertised accounting work** only with written bill-covering pay.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely loss of my high salary.
S2.quote: I can search and pay the mortgage for months, but I cannot make a good offer appear.
fieldNote: He sees on-site **stock counts** as a short bridge before robots around 2031, not a permanent refuge.
His strong reserve permits a search, but stock contracts require **childcare fit** and start dates.

steps.text: Redirect monthly car-upgrade deposits into new job-loss cash

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let me see whether the firm pays people to check AI mistakes. I could build that record while my current salary is coming in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm that the quality log should be public to staff and clients before 2031. AGI reaches account preparation then, and robots around 2034 are a separate problem for physical stock work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think the junior return job could vanish, but I could become the person who explains why a system made a tax error. I do not assume that work survives AGI; I want to see a funded role and actual clients before leaving this one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one paid error-review assignment each quarter only if Mara gives it to me, and use the firm’s paid quality course if a place is confirmed. I would keep adding fifty monthly from salary to cash; in the first year after 2031 I would move to a posted review position only if written pay and a start date cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the end of routine returns, but five years gives me a way to test the quality role. I would keep the present wage if no real review vacancy appears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would prove the role exists?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a budgeted place on the review team and a written job description, not a promise in a meeting. If there is no course place, I would study the firm’s free error examples while continuing my paid accounts work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy software yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I use the approved tools at work and do not want client data on my own laptop. I would spend time on real errors, not a personal subscription.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would take my children toward adulthood. I could build a long record without asking the mortgage to wait.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm should keep real junior practice and show clients its error record before AGI reaches accounts in 2036. Hands-on robots around 2039 come later and will not delay desk work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect ordinary return fees to fall, but at 53 I could have years of quality reviews and a full-year reserve. I would still want a posted role with a salary. A good record is not a contract.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep checking current tax files with approved AI and transfer fifty a month from salary until our reserve covers one year. I would take paid quality audits only if Mara assigns them; if my junior post contracts in the first year after 2036, I would take a posted review role only with written pay and a start date that cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the longer-term desk change, but our income looks stable for the next few years. Ten years gives me a chance to earn a record rather than buy a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you make a big investment now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would keep the reserve in cash and avoid buying a software licence for myself. Our family shop taught me to pay for tools only when they earn their cost.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children Sami and Lina to learn to check an answer, whatever tool produces it. I would also tell them that a paid apprenticeship is worth more than a shiny advert.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could remove my unusually good junior wage before another offer is real. Written job terms, a paid chance to do quality reviews, and a short income bridge if the search runs past our reserve would help. I would keep doing paid work while I looked.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether the firm will still teach people to question an AI result. A junior who only sees green ticks cannot learn which invoice is wrong. I want the error log left open for trainees.

headlineQuote: A junior who only sees green ticks cannot learn which invoice is wrong.
portrait: Ivan is a **43-year-old** junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree who checks shop accounts against receipts.
His junior pay is **high**, with ten months saved, a mortgage, two school-age children, and many nearby firms.
He uses **AI daily** but compares flags with original documents before Mara signs.
A **2028** desk loss alarms him despite strong reserves; temporary stock work may bridge a gap before robots.
Longer warning allows **assigned quality reviews**, paid learning, and new monthly deposits without leaving current pay.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his unusually high junior wage before a suitable offer appears.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written job terms**, assigned paid quality reviews, and an income bridge if the search outlasts savings.
